name: Card Bag
description: You have a bag which contains $$$n$$$ cards. There is a number written on each card; the number on $$$i$$$-th card is $$$a_i$$$. You are playing the following game. During each turn, you choose and remove a random card from the bag (all cards that are still left inside the bag are chosen equiprobably). Nothing else happens during the first turn — but during the next turns, after removing a card (let the number on it be $$$x$$$), you compare it with the card that was removed during the previous turn (let the number on it be $$$y$$$). Possible outcomes are: if $$$x \lt y$$$, the game ends and you lose; if $$$x = y$$$, the game ends and you win; if $$$x \gt y$$$, the game continues. If there are no cards left in the bag, you lose. Cards are not returned into the bag after you remove them. You have to calculate the probability of winning in this game. It can be shown that it is in the form of $$$\frac{P}{Q}$$$ where $$$P$$$ and $$$Q$$$ are non-negative integers and $$$Q \neq 0$$$, $$$P \le Q$$$. Output the value of $$$P \cdot Q^{−1} ~(mod ~~ 998244353)$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 5000$$$) — the number of cards in the bag. The second live contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le n$$$) — the $$$i$$$-th integer is the number written on the $$$i$$$-th card.
output_specification: Print one integer — the probability of winning in this game modulo $$$998244353$$$.
approach_summary: Formulate expectation as E[X] = ∑ P(e) * v(e). Formulate linear transition equations on states and solve via DAG DP or Gaussian elimination.
